hook: A U.S. Navy pilot flying a nighttime DCA mission on 27 October 2020 reported two metallic, balloon-shaped UAP at 26,000 feet that emitted red blinking strobes, were tracked on radar and FLIR, and vanished instantaneously while also triggering noise jamming indications.
why_it_matters: This report is notable for three concurrent, multi-sensor-confirmed anomalous characteristics reported together: a stable radar trackfile, two IR-significant contacts on the targeting pod, and an apparent instantaneous disappearance ('IN 1/30TH OF A SECOND, THEY WERE GONE'). The simultaneous noise jamming indication — not merely an anomalous flight behavior but an apparent electromagnetic effect on the aircraft's systems — elevates this beyond a typical misidentification. The document was formally approved for release to AARO in March 2026 under USCENTCOM MOR authority, placing it within the structured military UAP reporting and disclosure pipeline.

key_findings.finding: The pilot achieved radar lock and targeting pod video on the two contacts but could not close within 16.9 nautical miles for a better visual identification.

quotes.text: IOBTAINED RADAR LOCK AND TARGET POD VIDEO BUT UNABLE TO GET CLOSER THAN 16.9NM TID GETA BETTER ID.

key_findings.finding: The FLIR/targeting pod confirmed two infrared-significant contacts, one of which was observed circling the other before both vanished instantaneously.

quotes.text: THE TARGET POD SHOWED 2 IR SIGNIFICANT CONTACTS. ONE RANGE FOUL~ER WAS CIRCLING AROUND THE OTHER IN 1130TH OF A SECOND, THEY WERE GONE.

key_findings.finding: The pilot's visual tally described the objects as two red blinking strobes, while the form's checkboxes identified them as metallic, balloon-shaped, opaque, and reflective.

quotes.text: TALLY ACHIEVED WAS 2X RED BLINKING STROBES

key_findings.finding: The encounter included noise jamming indications on the pilot's aircraft, indicated by two chevrons — suggesting an active electronic effect associated with the UAP.

quotes.text: NOISE JAMMING WAS RECIEVED. NOISE JAMMING WAS INDICATED BY TWO CHEVRONS.

key_findings.finding: The mission was a DCA (Defense Counter Air) sortie flown at night at 26,000 feet, and the contacts were moving on a heading of 060 at 20 knots with a stable radar trackfile before their disappearance.

quotes.text: Was the contact moving? Yes Direction/Speed 060/20

legacy_program_connections.reasoning: The document is explicitly stamped 'Approved for Release to AARO' on 03/27/26 under USCENTCOM MOR authority, making AARO the direct institutional recipient of this report.

The SPEAR reporting system and standardized Range Fouler Debrief Form represent institutionalized UAP data collection infrastructure; Wright-Patterson has historically been associated with centralized U.S. military UAP analysis, though this document does not name it directly.
